key_insight: Direct structural evidence shows carrier-lattice distortion in lead-halide perovskites, but it does not yet prove large polaron formation or that polarons cause defect tolerance.
engineering_relevance: Device models and materials design should not assume polaron-based defect screening; instead, carrier transport and recombination must be interpreted through excitation-density-dependent lattice measurements.
method: Compare time-resolved structural probes with calculations of thermal lattice motion and carrier effective mass.
Contrast carrier-lattice coupling in 3D, Ruddlesden-Popper, and Dion-Jacobson perovskites.
Separate polaron screening of carrier-carrier scattering from true defect tolerance using transport and defect-response data.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites direct structural measurements, theoretical calculations, and new transport data that distinguish lattice distortion, scattering reduction, and defect tolerance.
watch_item: Polaron-like signatures observed at high ultrafast-experiment carrier densities may not represent the low-density operating conditions of solar cells.
paper_title: Polarons in Lead-Halide Perovskites: What the Structural Evidence Does and Does Not Establish
